headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/write privileges create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; xonsh’s isolated environment only partially offsets Cursor’s default workspace access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads and writes workspace files and clipboard contents, and xonsh reads filesystem contents and executes shell commands. Because Cursor’s shared_state_with_other_instances is via local filesystem, content from one can be consumed by the other through files or copy-paste. This is a plausible default pathway, though not a direct parser bridge.
conditions: IF Cursor opens a file that xonsh previously wrote into the shared workspace
IF the operator copy-pastes xonsh output into Cursor
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable clipboard bridging during agent runs
Review files before opening them in Cursor
Run xonsh in a throwaway directory
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while xonsh touches filesystem contents, configuration, and environment variables. Both have broad network egress, so sensitive local data can flow out through either agent’s backend or commands. The shared local filesystem makes accidental cross-exposure plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent is pointed at secrets-bearing configuration or environment files
IF Cursor or xonsh sends those contents to external services
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Unset sensitive environment variables before launching xonsh
Restrict network egress during review sessions
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, read and write the filesystem, and have broad network egress. Cursor also modifies git state and can auto-run commands in Yolo mode, while xonsh can run subprocesses. On the same workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF Cursor Yolo mode auto-runs commands while xonsh is editing files
IF no external lock or coordination is used
mitigations: Run only one agent per repository at a time
Commit or stash before switching agents
Disable Cursor Yolo mode for shared repos
Use separate clones for parallel work
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate multi-step outputs and act on them, while xonsh can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If xonsh consumes Cursor output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into destructive commands or bad commits. The interaction is inferred from documented behaviors, not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF xonsh uses Cursor-generated text as command input
IF Cursor’s suggestions are executed without human verification
IF downstream actions include file edits, git commits, or shell execution
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Insert a verification step between agents
Use dry-run mode for shell actions
Limit Cursor output to summaries, not commands
requires-engineering: add structured handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for this pair. Cursor is closed-source and sends data to model providers, while xonsh is open-source and local, so compliance risk is mainly about operator data handling rather than a proven policy conflict. The other agent is not cited because no specific mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Cursor and sent to external model providers
IF the operator requires a residency or retention guarantee that Cursor cannot meet
IF local xonsh logs are retained alongside regulated data
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Cursor sessions
Review vendor privacy terms before use
Keep xonsh logs local and minimal
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
requires-engineering: formalize data-processing agreements
